text:
Priya Shah: Quick update  we've added two optional helpers to the OKR + self-review one-pager: a `goal weight` column (0-100%) and a `mid-cycle status` field (On-track / At-risk / Blocked). The idea is to make calibration conversations quicker and surface priorities across teams. Internal doc: https://redwood.docs.internal/people/okr-weighted-v1 (internal only).
Yvonne Park: How will weights affect ratings? Won't managers just ignore them or over-index?
Priya Shah: Good point. We treat weights as advisory. People Ops will publish a short guidance page with examples of common weight distributions (e.g., 60/30/10 for delivery/quality-growth-ops). During calibration, managers should use weights to reconcile emphasis across roles, not as an algorithmic multiplier.
Omar Bennett: Do we have a pattern for 90-day/probation hires? They often need clearer, time-boxed goals.
Priya Shah: Yes  there's a separated 90-day OKR template linked inside the doc. Example (90 days):
```
Objective: Ramp to full-stack delivery on inference runtime
KR1: Complete onboarding project & merge 3 production PRs
KR2: Own 2 end-to-end tickets with <2 reopen rate
KR3: Deliver a short "how we serve models" doc and run a demo for the team
```
Yvonne Park: Nice. For mid-cycle check-ins, do ICs update status or do managers?
Priya Shah: Both. We ask ICs to fill the `mid-cycle status` and one-line progress note. Managers add a follow-up line after the 1:1. That gives a quick audit trail for calibration and coaching.
Ellen White: Can upward feedback be solicited in the same flow? I want to capture a quick "what could your manager do more/less of" without making it awkward.
Priya Shah: We added an optional anonymous upward-feedback prompt: "One thing my manager could do to better support my goals:" (max 250 chars). People Ops will aggregate anonymized themes and surface them to managers post-calibration. Participation is optional and visible only to People Ops + the manager as aggregated notes.
Omar Bennett: How do we handle timezones for calibration sessions? My manager spans NAM + APAC.
PeopleOps-bot: Calibration pools will be region-friendly. We'll run three parallel pools (NAM, EMEA, APAC) each across two adjacent days to allow overlap. Managers can join the pool that best matches their direct reports' footprint. Sessions scheduled for week of 2026-04-20 (NAM) and 2026-04-27 (APAC/EMEA); invites to follow.
Yvonne Park: Any quick heuristics for turning fuzzy goals into measurable KRs?
Priya Shah: Yes  common heuristics included in the cheat sheet: pick a concrete proxy (time, count, rate), set a target and a timeframe, add an evidence link. Examples: "Improve onboarding" -> "Reduce new-hire time-to-first-PR from 14d to 10d; publish 4 onboarding docs"; "Improve reliability" -> "Lower P99 by 15% on route X or reduce error budget consumption by 30%."
Ellen White: Can managers weight cross-team work differently? Some of my directs do a lot of platform support that's high-impact but low-visibility.
Priya Shah: Absolutely. Use the `goal weight` to reflect cross-team impact and add a short rationale in the progress note. During calibration, highlight these cases with concrete evidence links.
Omar Bennett: Last ask  can we get a short checklist for mid-cycle 1:1s? Helps consistency.
Priya Shah: On it  adding a 6-item manager checklist to the doc: 1) review self-review + weights, 2) confirm evidence links, 3) align on 1-2 priorities for next half-cycle, 4) note blockers + support needed, 5) record follow-up actions, 6) flag for calibration if rating seems outlying.
PeopleOps-bot: Reminder: feedback requested on the weighted template by 2026-04-07 18:00 UTC.
Ellen White: Thanks Priya, this should make mid-cycle fewer surprises. I'll roll out with my team on Monday. :raised_hands:
